newsitem.title: UK: Battersea power station to become cinema complex.
newsitem.headline: Battersea power station to become cinema complex.

text.p: Battersea power station, a crumbling monolith on the banks of the River Thames, is to be turned into what developers on Monday called the world's largest cinema complex.

Warner Village Cinemas said the building -- one of London's most famous 20th Century landmarks with its four huge white chimneys -- will include a 32-screen theatre with seating for over 8,000 people.

The 35 million pound ($56 million) scheme is the latest plan to rescue one of the world's largest brick buildings, a monument to Britain's pre-war industrial heritage, which has been falling into decay since it closed in 1983, half a century after it was built.

With its 31 acres of prime south-bank river frontage, it has attracted previous plans to turn it into a rival Disneyland but the only serious effort to develop the site foundered on huge repair costs in 1989.
Save Britain's Heritage charity has called it "the Mount Everest of conservation."

The joint venture between Warner Brothers International and Australia-based Village Roadshow Ltd to build what it calls a "Power Plex" is expected to create 400 new full and part-time jobs. Up to 7,000 people will be employed during the building stage which is expected to be finished in early 2000.
"The Power Plex will be the largest multiplex (cinema) in the world," Millard L. Ochs, president of Warner Bros International told a news conference at the power station.
Britain's National Heritage Secretary, Chris Smith, welcomed the development, saying it will help the new Labour government regenerate the Thames.
The cinema complex is the first stage of a retail and entertainment centre planned by Hong Kong-based Parkview International which acquired the site in 1993.

Parkview plans to build two hotels, two live performance theatres, film editing studios, showcase pavilions and offices and shops on the river site which will have a rail link to London's main Victoria train station. It will also be connected to a river taxi system.
